note: Kimi Code uses Moonshot models. Model selection is controlled via ~/.kimi-code/config.toml [model] section. Per-agent model switching is not yet supported; the squad should use the workspace default and accept the trade-off.

tier-s.rationale: k1.5 has the strongest reasoning for architecture and complex implementation. 128k context handles large codebases.

tier-a.rationale: Spec and QA require the same reasoning strength as design. k1.5 provides excellent structured output for EARS requirements.

tier-b.rationale: 32k context is sufficient for discovery and domain modeling in most slices. ~3x cheaper than 128k.

tier-c.rationale: 8k is adequate for lite agent tasks (≤3 files) and knowledge summarization. Lowest cost per token.

config_toml_example:
[model]
provider = 'moonshot'
model = 'kimi-k1.5'
# For cost-saving runs, temporarily switch to:
# model = 'moonshot-v1-32k'
